title: Staged model experiment control plane for hybrid rollouts
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Problem: We lack a single orchestration/control plane for staged model experiments that supports hybrid rollout modes (canary + A/B + shadow) with automated statistical checks and policy-driven auto-rollback. That gap forces ad-hoc scripts, inconsistent safety checks, and a higher cognitive load for PLG customers when promoting model versions across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Proposal: Ship a Staged Experiment Control Plane (SECP) — a lightweight control layer in the Console + runtime hooks that lets product teams define experiments declaratively. Core capabilities: exposure schedules, cohort and sample definitions, live sequential statistical tests (A/B and canary), shadow-only traffic routing, automatic rollback triggers (paired with runtime fallback), and per-experiment observability (metric deltas, confidence intervals, drift alerts). Experiments should be usable via the Console UI (experiment canvas) and a REST/SDK API for infra-as-code.

Key behaviors:
- Define experiments with variants: baseline (v1), candidate(s) (v2, v3), optional shadow variants.
- Exposure control: % traffic per cohort, time-windowed ramps, geo/region/capability filters.
- Statistical checks: sequential hypothesis testing (Wald SPRT or alpha-spending), minimum sample sizes per metric, configurable primary metric and guardrail metrics, and early-stop rules for signal/noise.
- Safety: automatic fallback to baseline on critical failures, configurable severity tiers for rollback (immediate, guarded, advisory).
- Observability: live CIs, per-token latency/cost deltas, error rates, hallucination proxies (toxicity/QA checks) surfaced in Console + alerts in PagerDuty/Slack.

Why hybrid: Many customers want to run shadow and canary together — e.g., send 5% canary traffic to v2 for real exposure while simultaneously streaming 100% shadow traffic to v3 for offline evals. SECP codifies that pattern and ensures consistent gating across deployments.

Non-goals: full experiment analysis suite (deep post-hoc analytics), auto-tuning model hyperparameters, replacing dedicated A/B analytics pipelines. SECP focuses on online gating and safety for rollouts.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Create/edit experiment in Console and via API with: variants, cohorts, exposure schedule, rollout window, primary and guardrail metrics.
2) Runtime routes traffic per experiment spec for Hosted and Dedicated; shadow routing for Private via telemetry integration.
3) Sequential statistical checks run realtime and produce pass/warn/fail states; early-stop triggers operate as configured.
4) Auto-rollback executes fallback policy in runtime and logs action to audit trail; rollback can be manually overridden.
5) Dashboard shows metric deltas, CIs, cumulative exposure, and links to raw traces/PRs.
6) Automated end-to-end e2e test validating a synthetic failure triggers rollback in <2 minutes.
7) Documentation and runbook published; two SEs trained and can run first pilot.
detailed_plan:
Phase 1 (design & API): finalize experiment spec (YAML/JSON schema), Console wireframes, and sequential test defaults. Phase 2 (runtime integration): runtime routing hooks, safe fallback API, eventing for metrics and audit logs. Phase 3 (observability): dashboard panels, alerting rules, and sample prompts/metric templates for common LOEs (latency, cost, toxicity proxies). Phase 4 (pilot): internal pilot with infra and search teams, iterate on thresholds and UX. Phase 5 (GA): docs, runbooks, SDK examples, open a public sample repo.

Engineering tickets: define experiment schema (ENG-47111), runtime routing + fallback (ENG-50234), metrics aggregation + sequential tester (ENG-48990), Console UX and dashboard (ENG-49812).

Rollout plan: alpha (internal-only) -> limited beta (2 customers on Dedicated) -> GA. Each phase gated by reliability metrics and a successful pilot rollback test.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives from noisy metrics cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: conservative defaults, require two independent signals or minimum exposure before critical rollback. Risk: complexity of supporting Private/on-prem metric shipping. Mitigation: pluggable telemetry adapters and a local evaluation agent for air-gapped installs. Risk: customers mis-configure primary metric. Mitigation: inline templates and a confirmation preview that simulates likely outcomes.
